authors: Xavier Gabaix, Ralph S. J. Koijen, Robert J. Richmond, Motohiro Yogo
title: Asset Embeddings
abstract_summary: Uses portfolio holdings to learn asset representations and connect those embeddings to demand, substitution, and equilibrium asset-pricing behavior.
why_it_matters: Core paper for reverse-engineering institutional decision logic from holdings. It reframes assets and investors as objects with learned latent positions, which is directly relevant to inferring demand, substitution, and investor-specific preference structure.

authors: Ralph S. J. Koijen, Motohiro Yogo
title: A Demand System Approach to Asset Pricing
venue: Journal of Political Economy / NBER Working Paper 21749
abstract_summary: Builds an asset-pricing demand system using investor-level portfolio holdings and market clearing to estimate elasticities and pricing effects.
why_it_matters: Load-bearing framework: it converts investor holdings into estimable demand curves. This is the cleanest academic bridge between observed portfolio positions and latent decision logic.

authors: Maarten P. Scholl, Mahmoud Mahfouz, Anisoara Calinescu, J. Doyne Farmer
title: Learning to Manage Investment Portfolios beyond Simple Utility Functions
abstract_summary: Uses learning-based portfolio-management methods to move beyond fixed mean-variance or simple utility objectives.
why_it_matters: Important because it questions the simple utility-function assumption behind many portfolio models. It fits the thesis that real investors optimize messy, multi-objective, path-dependent decision rules.

authors: Bryan T. Kelly, Boris Kuznetsov, Semyon Malamud, Teng Andrea Xu
title: Artificial Intelligence Asset Pricing Models
abstract_summary: Applies transformer-based AI models to stochastic discount factor estimation and compares pricing-error reductions to classical methods.
why_it_matters: Frontier ML asset-pricing work. Useful as a benchmark for when an AI model is genuinely pricing risk versus curve-fitting alpha labels.

authors: Xavier Gabaix, Ralph S. J. Koijen
title: In Search of the Origins of Financial Fluctuations: The Inelastic Markets Hypothesis
venue: Quarterly Journal of Economics / NBER Working Paper 28967
abstract_summary: Argues that aggregate demand shifts can move prices strongly when market demand curves are inelastic.
why_it_matters: Explains why flows can have large price impact. This is the economic reason investor-decision inference matters: demand shocks do not get harmlessly absorbed in perfectly elastic markets.

title: QLBS Q-Learner Goes NuQLear: Fitted Q Iteration, Inverse RL, and Option Pricing
abstract_summary: Extends the QLBS framework using fitted Q-iteration and inverse-RL ideas for derivatives and hedging.
why_it_matters: Shows how option pricing, hedging, and RL can be put in the same control framework. Good bridge from mathematical finance to RL implementation.

title: G-Learner and GIRL: Goal-Based Wealth Management with Reinforcement Learning and Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract_summary: Applies RL and IRL to infer and optimize goal-based wealth-management objectives.
why_it_matters: One of the clearest finance-specific IRL papers. It targets investor objective inference rather than only return prediction.

authors: Jacobo Roa-Vicens, Cyrine Chtourou, Angelos Filos, Francisco Rullan, Yarin Gal, Ricardo Silva
title: Towards Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Limit Order Book Dynamics
abstract_summary: Explores how IRL can infer latent objectives underlying limit-order-book dynamics.
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to recovering agent objectives from order-book behavior. It is more aligned with execution/microstructure than portfolio-level utility inference.

authors: Jon Hendricks, Daniel Harmon, Umut Demirel, Chang Yun, Daniel P. Sanderson, Douglas L. T. Rohde
title: Inferring Agent Objectives at Different Scales of a Complex System
abstract_summary: Studies inference of latent agent objectives across multiple scales in complex systems.
why_it_matters: Useful for multi-scale objective inference. Trading systems have micro-objectives at order level and macro-objectives at portfolio level; this paper frames that scale problem.

authors: Sinong Geng, Houssam Nassif, Carlos Manzanares, Andrew Jaegle, Samy Bengio
title: Deep PQR: Solving Inverse Reinforcement Learning using Anchor Actions
abstract_summary: Presents an IRL method using anchor actions to recover rewards in complex environments.
why_it_matters: Not finance-specific, but useful when demonstrations are sparse or ambiguous. Anchor-action structure maps well to constrained action spaces in execution and rebalancing.

title: Algorithms for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract_summary: Introduces algorithms for recovering reward functions from expert demonstrations.
why_it_matters: The foundation. It defines the original IRL problem: infer the reward function that explains observed expert behavior.

title: Apprenticeship Learning via Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract_summary: Shows how to learn policies from expert demonstrations by matching feature expectations.
why_it_matters: Important for imitation from demonstrations. The closest analogue in finance is learning from expert trade trajectories or manager holdings.

authors: Brian D. Ziebart, Andrew L. Maas, J. Andrew Bagnell, Anind K. Dey
title: Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract_summary: Introduces maximum-entropy formulation for probabilistic reward inference from demonstrations.
why_it_matters: Critical because it handles non-unique explanations of behavior by preferring maximum-entropy distributions. Finance needs this because multiple motives can explain the same trade.

title: Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract_summary: Uses Bayesian inference to estimate posterior distributions over reward functions.
why_it_matters: A natural fit for markets because reward inference should carry uncertainty. Useful for avoiding overconfident claims about an investor's objective.

title: Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning
abstract_summary: Formulates imitation learning as adversarial training between policy and discriminator.
why_it_matters: The modern imitation-learning anchor. It connects adversarial learning with occupancy-measure matching, useful for trade-sequence imitation.

authors: Stephane Ross, Geoffrey Gordon, Drew Bagnell
title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
abstract_summary: Introduces Dataset Aggregation for robust imitation learning under distribution shift.
why_it_matters: DAgger addresses compounding errors from pure behavioral cloning. In trading agents, small early errors compound into very different positions and exposure.

authors: Chelsea Finn, Sergey Levine, Pieter Abbeel
title: Guided Cost Learning: Deep Inverse Optimal Control via Policy Optimization
abstract_summary: Combines cost learning with policy optimization for inverse optimal control.
why_it_matters: Useful for high-dimensional reward learning when the cost function is unknown. Good conceptual link to inferring non-linear investor objectives.

authors: Justin Fu, Katie Luo, Sergey Levine
title: Learning Robust Rewards with Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract_summary: Introduces adversarial inverse reinforcement learning with more transferable recovered rewards.
why_it_matters: AIRL separates reward recovery from policy imitation more cleanly than vanilla GAIL. That matters if the goal is to infer decision logic, not merely copy behavior.

authors: Florian Tramer, Fan Zhang, Ari Juels, Michael K. Reiter, Thomas Ristenpart
title: Stealing Machine Learning Models via Prediction APIs
abstract_summary: Shows how prediction APIs can leak enough information to reconstruct model behavior.
why_it_matters: Foundational model-extraction paper. Relevant as a conceptual analogue to reverse-engineering decision policies from external observable behavior.

authors: Nicolas Papernot, Patrick McDaniel, Ian Goodfellow, Somesh Jha, Z. Berkay Celik, Ananth Grama
title: Practical Black-Box Attacks against Machine Learning
abstract_summary: Develops substitute-model methods for attacking black-box ML systems.
why_it_matters: Important for black-box query learning. In finance, the equivalent is querying/observing reactions and reconstructing latent policies under limited feedback.

title: Stealing Part of a Production Language Model
abstract_summary: Demonstrates extraction of part of a production-scale language model under black-box access.
why_it_matters: Current-generation model-extraction example. It shows that partial extraction of high-capacity systems can be practical under specific leakage channels.

authors: Kalpesh Krishna, Gaurav Singh Tomar, Ankur P. Parikh, Nicolas Papernot, Mohit Iyyer
title: Thieves on Sesame Street! Model Extraction of BERT-based APIs
abstract_summary: Studies extraction attacks against BERT-based prediction services.
why_it_matters: Useful for NLP/LLM agent settings. It covers extraction of behavior from black-box text APIs, relevant to competitor-agent monitoring.

title: Yes, My LoRD: Lower-Dimensional Subspace Discovery for Efficient Model Extraction
abstract_summary: Proposes lower-dimensional subspace discovery methods for more efficient model extraction.
why_it_matters: Recent model-extraction work focused on efficiency. Relevant when the observed system is too expensive to query exhaustively.

authors: Yanou Ramon, R. A. Farrokhnia, Sandra C. Matz, David Martens
title: Explainable AI for Psychological Profiling from Financial Transaction Records
abstract_summary: Uses explainable machine learning to infer psychological profiles from financial transaction data.
why_it_matters: Not trading-specific but directly relevant to inferring psychological traits from financial records. Useful for thinking about what can and cannot be inferred from transaction traces.

title: Narrative Economics
venue: American Economic Review / NBER Working Paper 23075
abstract_summary: Develops a research agenda for studying contagious economic narratives and their market/macroeconomic consequences.
why_it_matters: Important for news/story-driven flows. It gives a framework for how narratives can propagate and affect economic decisions.

authors: Thomas Henning, Siddhartha M. Ojha, Ross Spoon, Jiatong Han, Colin F. Camerer
title: LLM Trading: Analysis of LLM Agent Behavior in Experimental Asset Markets
abstract_summary: Analyzes how LLM agents behave in controlled experimental asset markets.
why_it_matters: Important because it studies LLM agents as market participants, not just text summarizers. Good for evaluating whether LLM decision behavior is stable under trading incentives.

title: Can Large Language Models Trade?
abstract_summary: Evaluates whether LLMs can generate trading-relevant signals or decisions.
why_it_matters: Directly tests the central hype claim. Use it as an empirical checkpoint before building agentic trading systems around LLM reasoning.

authors: Ryuji Hashimoto, Takehiro Takayanagi, Masahiro Suzuki, Kiyoshi Izumi
title: Agent-Based Simulation of a Financial Market with Large Language Model-Based Agents
abstract_summary: Builds a financial-market simulation populated by LLM-based agents.
why_it_matters: Relevant to market simulation with LLM agents. Useful for separating agent believability from actual alpha.

title: Behavioral Consistency Validation for LLM Agents
abstract_summary: Proposes methods to validate behavioral consistency in LLM agents.
why_it_matters: Critical for production agent systems: a trading agent that changes behavior under prompt perturbation is not a strategy, it is a liability.

title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
abstract_summary: Presents a multi-agent LLM framework for financial trading analysis and decision-making.
why_it_matters: Representative multi-agent LLM trading framework. Useful as a competitor/architecture reference, not as proof of profitable execution.

authors: Yang Li, Yangyang Yu, Haohang Li, Zhi Chen, Khaldoun Khashanah
title: TradingGPT: Multi-Agent System with Layered Memory and Distinct Characters for Enhanced Financial Trading Performance
abstract_summary: Uses a multi-agent LLM system with layered memory for financial trading decisions.
why_it_matters: Early LLM trading-agent architecture with memory and role separation. Useful as a baseline for what agent frameworks usually overclaim.

title: FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design
abstract_summary: Builds a financial trading agent with layered memory mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Important memory-based LLM trader reference. Good for comparing retrieval/memory against deterministic feature stores.

title: Trading-R1: Financial Trading with LLM Reasoning
abstract_summary: Applies reasoning-oriented LLM methods to trading workflows.
why_it_matters: Relevant because reasoning-tuned LLMs are being applied to trading. Treat as experimental until execution-cost and live-trading validation are shown.

title: QuantAgent: Seeking Holy Grail in Trading by Self-Improving Large Language Model
abstract_summary: Proposes a self-improving LLM agent for quantitative trading tasks.
why_it_matters: Useful as a self-improving agent architecture reference. Needs skepticism: self-improvement can easily become overfit backtest search.

title: Automate Strategy Finding with LLM in Quant Investment
abstract_summary: Uses LLMs to automate parts of quantitative strategy discovery.
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to automated strategy discovery. Pair with backtest-overfitting papers before trusting any generated strategy.

title: GPT-Signal: Generative AI for Semi-Automatic Feature Engineering in the Alpha Research Process
abstract_summary: Uses GPT-style systems to assist feature engineering in alpha research.
why_it_matters: High practical relevance: LLMs may be better at feature ideation than autonomous trading. This is closer to a credible alpha-research workflow.

title: Large Language Model Agent in Financial Trading: A Survey
abstract_summary: Surveys LLM-agent systems and tasks in financial trading.
why_it_matters: Useful map of the LLM trading-agent literature. Read after the primary papers to avoid swallowing survey framing uncritically.

title: TraderTalk: Analyzing Large Language Model Behavior in Simulated Financial Markets
abstract_summary: Studies LLM behavior and communication in simulated financial markets.
why_it_matters: Relevant for observing LLM strategic behavior in simulated markets. Useful for testing whether agent conversations add signal or only narrative.

authors: Maria del Rio-Chanona, Marco Pangallo, Cars Hommes
title: Can Generative AI Agents Behave Like Humans? An Evaluation of Generative AI Agents in Generic Decision-Making Tasks
abstract_summary: Evaluates generative AI agents on generic human decision-making tasks.
why_it_matters: Needed to test whether LLM agents are valid behavioral stand-ins. Market simulations fail if the agents are not behaviorally calibrated.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
abstract_summary: Introduces memory/reflection/planning agents that simulate believable human behavior.
why_it_matters: The general agent-simulation ancestor for many financial agent ideas. Useful for architecture, not financial validity.

authors: Peer Nagy, Jan-Peter Calliess, Stefan Zohren
title: Asynchronous Deep Double Duelling Q-Learning for Trading-Signal Execution in Limit Order Book Markets
abstract_summary: Applies asynchronous double dueling Q-learning to LOB trading-signal execution.
why_it_matters: Important because it focuses on execution in LOB markets rather than abstract buy/sell labels. That is closer to real tradability.

authors: Yufei Huang, Junyi Zhou, Di Song
title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Portfolio Management
abstract_summary: Applies deep reinforcement learning to portfolio management and allocation.
why_it_matters: Useful portfolio RL baseline. Read as an implementation reference, not a profitability proof.

authors: Zhengyao Jiang, Dixing Xu, Jinjun Liang
title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for the Financial Portfolio Management Problem
abstract_summary: Builds a deep RL framework for portfolio allocation over multiple assets.
why_it_matters: Widely cited RL portfolio framework. Good for understanding the early architecture pattern and its limitations.

title: Planning with Diffusion for Flexible Behavior Synthesis
abstract_summary: Introduces diffusion models as trajectory planners for offline RL/control.
why_it_matters: Not finance-specific, but diffusion planning is relevant for offline policy generation. Could be adapted to execution or portfolio trajectories.

title: Is Conditional Generative Modeling all you need for Decision Making?
abstract_summary: Uses conditional generative modeling for decision-making trajectories.
why_it_matters: Decision Diffuser is relevant to offline decision making from historical trajectories. Finance application requires strict leakage and regime controls.

title: Diffusion World Models
abstract_summary: Combines diffusion modeling with world-model approaches for decision making.
why_it_matters: Useful for model-based RL concepts. For markets, the danger is learning a beautiful world model of stale regimes.

authors: Rama Cont, Arseniy Kukanov, Sasha Stoikov
title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
abstract_summary: Studies how order-book events and order-flow imbalance affect price changes.
why_it_matters: Load-bearing microstructure paper. It quantifies order-flow imbalance and price impact better than retail concepts like fair value gaps.

title: High-frequency market-making with inventory constraints and directional bets
abstract_summary: Studies high-frequency market making with inventory risk and directional expectations.
why_it_matters: Useful extension of market-making models. Connects inventory constraints with directional views.

title: How to Correctly Apply Bellman Equation to Avellaneda-Stoikov Market-Making Model
abstract_summary: Revisits the Bellman-equation treatment of the Avellaneda-Stoikov model.
why_it_matters: Recent correction/critique around a widely used market-making model. Useful because many implementations copy formulas without checking assumptions.

title: On the Evolution of Cryptocurrency Market Efficiency
abstract_summary: Tests adaptive market efficiency in cryptocurrency markets.
why_it_matters: Shows AMH-style testing in crypto. Useful for regime-specific market-efficiency analysis.

title: A Test of the Adaptive Market Hypothesis using a Time-Varying AR Model in Japan
abstract_summary: Uses time-varying autoregression to test adaptive market behavior in Japan.
why_it_matters: Example of testing AMH with time-varying predictability. Useful for building simple regime-drift diagnostics.

authors: Luyang Chen, Markus Pelger, Jason Zhu
title: Deep Learning in Asset Pricing
abstract_summary: Uses deep learning to estimate stochastic discount factors and expected returns.
why_it_matters: Core deep-learning asset-pricing paper. It is a stronger baseline than generic LSTM trading demos.

authors: Bryan T. Kelly, Boris Kuznetsov, Semyon Malamud, Teng Andrea Xu
title: Artificial Intelligence Asset Pricing Models
abstract_summary: Applies transformer-based AI models to stochastic discount factor estimation.
why_it_matters: Cross-listed from Group A because it is also the frontier AI asset-pricing anchor.

authors: Matthew Dixon, Nicholas G. Polson, Maria Goicoechea
title: Deep Partial Least Squares for Conditional Asset Pricing
abstract_summary: Combines partial least squares ideas with deep learning for conditional asset pricing.
why_it_matters: Useful method paper for high-dimensional conditional pricing. Relevant when feature space is large but economic interpretation matters.

title: Deep Learning for Conditional Asset Pricing Models
abstract_summary: Applies deep-learning methods to conditional asset-pricing models.
why_it_matters: Recent conditional asset-pricing work. Use as frontier scan, not a primary foundation until authors/version are verified.

title: The Impact of Uncertainty in Machine Learning Predictions on Asset Pricing
abstract_summary: Studies how predictive uncertainty from ML models affects asset-pricing conclusions.
why_it_matters: Useful because uncertainty estimates matter for sizing and risk, not just point forecasts.

authors: D. Lemmens, L. Z. Cheng, S. Wang, A. L. Baaquie
title: A Path Integral Approach to Option Pricing with Stochastic Volatility
abstract_summary: Applies path-integral methods to stochastic-volatility option pricing.
why_it_matters: Useful as alternative mathematical machinery for option pricing. Not core for a trading startup unless modeling derivatives directly.

title: Option Pricing with Stochastic Volatility, Equity Premium, and Interest Rates
abstract_summary: Studies option-pricing models incorporating stochastic volatility, equity premium, and interest rates.
why_it_matters: Recent option-pricing scan. Useful for understanding models that combine volatility, equity risk premia, and rates.

authors: Peter Carr, Marcos Lopez de Prado
title: Determining Optimal Trading Rules without Backtesting
abstract_summary: Derives trading rules using analytical methods instead of traditional backtest selection.
why_it_matters: Important because it attacks the usual backtest-mining loop. Useful for strategy design that starts from optimal stopping/control rather than brute-force search.

title: Revisiting the Stylized Facts of Financial Time Series
abstract_summary: Revisits empirical stylized facts of financial time series using modern data.
why_it_matters: Recent audit of classic stylized facts. Useful because market microstructure and electronic trading may alter old empirical regularities.

authors: Rama Cont, Arseniy Kukanov, Sasha Stoikov
title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
abstract_summary: Quantifies how different order-book events contribute to price impact.
why_it_matters: Cross-listed because it is the academic version of order-flow imbalance. This is the paper to read before ICT-style claims.

title: Pattern Recognition in Micro-Trading Behaviors before Stock Price Jumps
abstract_summary: Studies patterns in micro-level trading behavior before price jumps.
why_it_matters: Useful because it moves pattern recognition into micro-trading behavior rather than subjective chart labels.

title: Long Short-Term Memory Pattern Recognition in Currency Trading: Identifying Wyckoff Accumulation and Distribution Phases
abstract_summary: Uses LSTM-style pattern recognition for currency-trading phases inspired by Wyckoff concepts.
why_it_matters: Interesting but lower-anchor quality. Treat as an example of trying to operationalize discretionary pattern concepts with sequence models.

title: Fake Prediction Markets, Real Confidence Signals
abstract_summary: Studies whether simulated/fake prediction markets can still reveal confidence signals.
why_it_matters: Recent AI/prediction-market frontier paper. Useful for separating market format from the confidence signal extracted from participants.

title: Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Effects of Investor Beliefs and Strategies on Kalshi and Polymarket
abstract_summary: Analyzes crowd wisdom in Kalshi and Polymarket using trader beliefs and strategies.
why_it_matters: Current and directly relevant to real prediction markets. Useful for comparing belief aggregation versus strategy effects.

title: Prediction Arena: A Benchmark for LLM Forecasting over Prediction Markets
abstract_summary: Benchmarks LLM forecasting performance on prediction-market-style tasks.
why_it_matters: Useful benchmark reference for LLM forecasting. It ties AI forecasting to market-like evaluation.

title: LiveTradeBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Real-Time Financial Forecasting and Trading
abstract_summary: Benchmarks LLMs on real-time financial forecasting and trading tasks.
why_it_matters: Important because static benchmark results are weaker than real-time forecasting. Useful for live evaluation harness design.

title: Pattern Recognition in Micro-Trading Behaviors before Stock Price Jumps
abstract_summary: Studies micro-trading behavior patterns preceding price jumps.
why_it_matters: Best fit for rigorous pattern recognition at micro level. It focuses on observable behavior before jumps rather than discretionary chart annotation.

title: Replicating Financial Market Dynamics with a Simple Self-Improvement Mechanism for AI Traders
abstract_summary: Uses AI traders in a multi-agent market model to reproduce stylized market dynamics.
why_it_matters: Useful for agent-based market simulation. It links trader learning behavior to emergent market dynamics such as volatility clustering.

title: An Agent-Based Model for Designing a Financial Market that Works Well
abstract_summary: Uses agent-based modeling to study financial-market design and dynamics.
why_it_matters: Useful for connecting micro decision rules to market-level outcomes. Relevant for simulation-first quant research.

title: Long Short-Term Memory Pattern Recognition in Currency Trading
abstract_summary: Uses LSTMs to identify Wyckoff-style accumulation/distribution phases in currency data.
why_it_matters: Lower priority example of applying sequence models to classical pattern language. Use only as a sandbox idea, not as evidence of robust edge.
